title: tests: exit on INT and TERM in suites that stub privileged commands
body:
Three suites that keep fake sudo, mnexec or iperf on PATH removed them in a signal handler that then returned, so after INT or TERM the suite ran on and later calls reached the real commands.

- The handlers now only exit, with 130 or 143; the EXIT trap does the cleanup.
- The probe-stub closing check tells a stub that was never installed from one deleted while the suite ran, with a mutation case for the second.

title: p4 testbed, link telemetry: act only on manifests they can trust
body:
The link telemetry emitter and the P4 testbed reaper act only on a manifest they can trust, and only on the exact process it names.

- Manifests are read through a trust check: owned by root or by the reader, and not writable by group or others. A manifest that fails it is refused with the reason.
- A process is identified by its exact argv and start time, not by a name substring.
- A bring-up whose switch manifest cannot be written now fails.
- Exercise fixtures record the compile command of each build artifact.
- New unit tests and mutation gates.

title: kernel: carry P4 switch capabilities onto get_graph_data nodes
body:
Lets a consumer (the Web-GUI) grey out operations a P4 switch cannot be asked to do.

- Each bmv2 switch node on /ndt/get_graph_data carries the capabilities object the proxy serves on GET /p4/switch_state, copied verbatim. The key is absent on OVS fabrics, before the first answer, and whenever the last 1 Hz read failed; absence means every operation is supported.
- One proxy request per tick feeds both the capabilities and the liveness verdicts (pollP4SwitchState).
- The L4 OVS/P4 differential allows the P4-only key; the contract spec pins its type.
- New unit tests, a wiring check and mutation gates.

title: ndt: tell a refused sudo grant from one it cannot read
body:
ndt status reported a sudo grant as granted whenever the probe exited non-zero without a recognised refusal.

- The probe reads sudo own "sudo:" diagnostics: a known refusal is refused, an unrecognised one is could-not-tell, listed non-fatal warnings are skipped.
- ndt status --check fails on a refused or untestable grant.
- What the rule still reads as granted (a silent refusal, a non-sudo: prefix) is recorded as KNOWN-ISSUES G-59 and pinned by control tests.

title: round.env: name the checkout it is in
body:
The E and F-5 round.env files hard-coded the main checkout, so suites and gates run from a worktree or a clone read and wrote the main checkout.

- KERNEL_DIR is derived from the file location; an exported absolute KERNEL_DIR still overrides. Non-bash, file-less and relative sourcing are refused.
- PY_PROXY can be overridden; a missing interpreter is now a failure in test_cell_gate_suspect_wiring, not a silent skip.
- Live E and F-5 runs refuse, before any write, when KERNEL_DIR is not the tree the lab helper runs.
- New suites and mutation gates for both.

title: ci: the Python L1 lane on a hosted runner
body:
Makes the Python L1 lane readable on a GitHub runner without silencing the lab.

- A test file may declare what it needs (`# NDTWIN_L1_NEEDS: ryu`); the lane probes the machine and excuses a skip only on a hosted CI runner that lacks the need. Anywhere else, and on any file that also failed a check, a skip is still a failure.
- P4 cases that need NDTwin compiled program skip when it is not built; the lane reports them as PROVED LESS only when it sees the artefacts are missing.
- CI checks out full history and builds p4_proxy/venv.
- test_grpc_port_block follows grpc_port(<name>) and allowlists the tutorials port lines; test_ndt_ovs_topo_script runs without a lab install; the NTG testbed_topo.py comparison in test_ovs4_sflow is retired.

title: ci: clang and TSan jobs green
body:
Fixes the two red C++ jobs.

- DeviceConfigurationAndPowerManager: the destructor is virtual. Tests derive from the class and main.cpp destroys it as itself, so clang rejected the non-virtual destructor under -Werror.
- utils::formatTime: localtime_r instead of localtime. getFlowInfoJson calls it from concurrent readers, which raced on the process-wide struct tm (TSan). New tests in test_IpToString.cpp.
- test_KernelStopIsBounded: the fixture closes its listening socket only after joining the accept thread (TSan).

title: B-2b analysed the accidental quote and not the deliberate one
body:
The entry describes what happens when a single quote lands in a match value by
accident: /bin/sh syntax error, curl never runs, and the kernel reports "no
response from <component>" -- blaming a healthy component with a message
indistinguishable from a real outage. That analysis is good and stands.

What it never asks is what happens when someone puts the quote there on purpose.
The quote does not corrupt the string, it ends it, and everything after it is a
command. The chain is entirely made of pieces already documented here: the
listener binds tcp::v4() -- 0.0.0.0, not loopback -- at
ControllerAndOtherEventHandler.cpp:90; northbound match values reach the
southbound body, which is B-2b's own worked example; json::dump() does not
escape a single quote, self-admitted at HttpRoutingStrategyBase.cpp:76-84; and
execCommand is a bare popen(), so it goes through /bin/sh. Anyone who can reach
port 8000 can run commands as the kernel's user. Fourteen southbound curl sites
share the construction.

The reason it read as a diagnostics problem for four rounds is one sentence in
the entry: "TE app currently only sends numbers and IPs, so it will not occur
naturally." That is a claim about accidents being used to rate the whole issue.
How often a bug fires by accident is set by normal use; how often it fires on
purpose is set by whether anyone wants it to. The two have nothing to do with
each other. Any entry that reasons about a malformed input needs to be asked the
second question explicitly.

Fix and its shape are unchanged -- one argv-based executor for every call site,
as both source comments already insist. Do not escape at one site; that would
make the other thirteen look handled. Only the priority changes.

Found by DeepSeek while specifying the chaos harness action surface; I verified
all four links against the source rather than relaying them. It did not find a
new defect, it found the half of an existing entry that was never written.

Also lands: the chaos harness action surface (DeepSeek, 45 actions with file:line
grounding) and oracle (Muse Spark, 8 invariants, 13 defect signatures, 13-item
anti-oracle), plus the auditor's load sampler from this morning's block.

[Co-developed with claude code -- Adam]
